name: ein
_comment: Ein surface-language TextMate grammar (S1.7c.8). REGEX highlighting,
not a parser: it will happily colour syntactically-invalid ein — shape
correctness is the loader's job (ein_ir::from_ir). The three closed reserved
name sets below are the single source of truth's mirror — keep them in
re-derives each list from this file and fails on drift. Since M1f S1f.5.5's
swap (2026-11-09) names follow the name rule (S1f.5.4): a name or a variable
is a run of ASCII name characters, digits among them, so there is no number
scope, a head ends at a space or a paren, and a bare _ or ?_ is invalid.

declarator-relation.comment: (relation R A B …) — head + relation-type name. Closed declarator set; see 06_reserved_names.md.

declarator-rule.comment: (rule N …) / (hrule N …) / (macro N …) — head + declared name.

primitive-form.comment: Rule-body / ⊥ structural primitives plus the `open` verdict atom, head position only (primitives.STRUCTURAL + RESERVED). `forall`/`unknown` are stdlib macros since P1.8 S1.5.9, not primitives; the macro spelled `open` was renamed `unknown` in M1d P1d.2 so the word could be the KB-level verdict.

equality-form.comment: (= a b …) — the `=` head, a name since M1f S1f.5.5's swap (S1f.5.4's name rule), coloured as the equality relation it is by convention.

paren.comment: Generic S-expression — any non-reserved head (a fact or a relation reference). Must come AFTER every specific head rule above.

keyword.comment: Any :keyword (KEYWORD terminal): `:` and a run of name characters. Each form takes a fixed set since M1f S1f.5.5's swap (S1f.5.11) and the parser refuses any other; every one is coloured.
keyword.name: entity.other.attribute-name.ein

boolean.comment: Bare true / false config values (the primitive `(false)` head is handled by #primitive-form before this is reached).
boolean.name: constant.language.boolean.ein

variable.comment: ?var pattern variable (VAR terminal): `?` and a run of name characters (the name rule, M1f S1f.5.4), so ?R*, ?_x and ?a.b are variables.
variable.name: variable.parameter.ein

wildcard.comment: A bare _ or ?_ (UNDERSCORE, VARUNDERSCORE): no production takes either since M1f S1f.5.5's swap (S1f.5.1's ruling), so each is marked invalid. A _ inside a name (House_1, ?_x, __closed__) is part of the name and never reaches here.
wildcard.name: invalid.illegal.underscore.ein
